answer: Sybil resistance comes from binding each agent identity to a cryptographically attested enclave measurement, MRENCLAVE, and requiring fresh verifier challenges before accepting its messages. Remote attestation proves that the approved code runs inside genuine SGX or SEV hardware, so copying a virtual-machine image cannot create another valid identity; under a one-identity-per-platform policy, cloning identities requires purchasing physical silicon. A pulse, nadir, or tundra deployment still faces this hardware-bound cost.
